What is petrified wood?

It is wood that turned to stone after being buried, as minerals slowly replaced every single part of it!

Ano ang petrified wood?

Ito ay kahoy na naging bato matapos matabunan, dahil unti-unting napalitan ng mineral ang bawat bahagi nito!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang petrified wood?

Mao kini ang kahoy nga nahimong bato human matabunan, kay hinay-hinay nga gipulihan sa mineral ang matag bahin niini!

Is most of Earth's water okay for us to drink?

Nope! Most of Earth's water is salty seawater. Only a small part is fresh water that we can actually drink!
copy.tl:
Karamihan ba sa tubig sa Mundo ay pwedeng inumin natin?

Hindi! Karamihan ng tubig sa Mundo ay maalat na tubig-dagat. Kakaunti lang ang sariwang tubig na maaari nating inumin!
copy.bis:
Kadaghanan ba sa tubig sa Kalibutan pwede nato mainom?

Dili! Kadaghanan sa tubig sa Kalibutan parat nga tubig-dagat. Gamay ra ang tab-ang nga tubig nga atong mainom!

copy.tl: Ang air resistance ay friction sa pagitan ng gumagalaw na bagay at hangin! Pinapabagal nito ang mga nahuhulog at ginagamit ito ng parachute para sa skydiver.
copy.bis: Ang air resistance usa ka friction taliwala sa nagalihok nga butang ug hangin! Nagpahinay kini sa mga nahulog ug gigamit sa parachute aron mapahinay ang skydiver.

copy.en: Sandpaper is awesome! It uses friction to scrape away rough spots and make bumpy wood feel perfectly smooth.
copy.tl: Ang papel de liha ay napakagaling! Gumagamit ito ng friction para gasgasin at gawing makinis ang magaspang na kahoy.
copy.bis: Ang papel de liha nindot kaayo! Naggamit kini ug friction aron gasgason ug himoong hamis ang magaspang nga kahoy.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how friction can produce heat and investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that friction causes wear and damage over time. It does not demonstrate friction producing heat, nor does it investigate ways of reducing or increasing friction, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Why do shoe soles and tires get damaged over time?

Over time, friction wears them down! It slowly damages things like your shoe soles and car tires.
copy.tl:
Bakit nauubos at nasisira ang suwelas ng sapatos at gulong sa paglipas ng panahon?

Sa paglipas ng panahon, nauubos at nasisira sila dahil sa friction!
copy.bis:
Nganong nahurot ug nadaot ang lapalapa sa sapatos ug ligid sa paglabay sa panahon?

Sa paglabay sa panahon, maghurot ug magdaot sila tungod sa friction!

copy.tl: May espesyal na likido na tinatawag na refrigerant na umiikot sa ref at nagdadala ng init palabas!
copy.bis: Adunay espesyal nga likido nga gitawag og refrigerant nga moliyok sa ref ug nagdala sa kainit pagawas!

copy.en: A frog doesn't always jump the same way — it makes small hops when moving slowly, but much bigger leaps when scared or escaping.
copy.tl: Hindi laging pareho ang lukso ng palaka — maliit na hop lang kapag dahan-dahan itong gumagalaw, pero mas malaki at malayong leap kapag natatakot o tumatakas.
copy.bis: Dili kanunay managsama ang lukso sa baki — gamay ra nga hop kon hinay kining molihok, apan mas dako ug layo nga lukso kon mahadlok o moikyas.

copy.tl: Karaniwang mas aktibo ang mga palaka sa gabi at nagtatago sa malamig na lugar kung araw.
copy.bis: Kasagaran mas aktibo ang mga baki sa gabii ug magtago sa bugnaw nga dapit kon adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: water vapor in the air turns straight into ice crystals on a leaf or window
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a frost-formation phenomenon tied to cold weather, but it does not teach identifying weather characteristics such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, or cloud cover. It only mentions cold and water vapor incidentally.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: water vapor in the air turns straight into ice crystals on a leaf or window
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes deposition (vapor to ice), a change of state, but the competency specifically requires describing melting, evaporation, freezing, and condensation using diagrams and flowcharts. The card does not use diagrams/flowcharts and does not address the listed processes; deposition is not among them.

copy.en:
Does frost always start as liquid water?

Nope! When it's very cold, water vapor in the air turns straight into ice crystals on a leaf or window — no droplets needed! That's why frost makes beautiful lacy patterns.
copy.tl:
Laging dumadaan ba sa tubig ang frost?

Hindi! Kapag napakalamig, ang singaw ng tubig sa hangin ay direktang nagiging kristal ng yelo sa dahon o salamin — walang patak! Kaya gumagawa ang frost ng magagandang disenyong yelo.
copy.bis:
Kanunay ba moagi sa tubig ang frost?

Dili! Kon bugnaw kaayo, ang alisngaw sa tubig sa hangin mahimong direkta nga kristal sa yelo sa dahon o bildo — walay tulo! Maong matahum ang disenyo sa frost.

assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on frost and snow as states of water, but does not describe changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) and does not use diagrams or flowcharts as required by the competency.

copy.en: Frost and snow are different! Frost grows right on cold surfaces like grass, while snow forms in clouds and falls down. Frost never falls—it just grows where it is!
copy.tl: Magkaiba ang frost at niyebe! Ang frost ay tumutubo mismo sa malamig na ibabaw tulad ng damo, habang ang niyebe ay nahuhulog mula sa ulap. Hindi nahuhulog ang frost!
copy.bis: Lahi ang frost ug niyebe! Ang frost motubo mismo sa bugnaw nga ibabaw sama sa balili, samtang ang niyebe mahulog gikan sa panganod. Ang frost dili mahulog!

copy.tl: Mahilig magkasama ang mga paniki — libu-libo sa kanila ang maaaring magtipon sa iisang puno lang, kaya isang malaking roost ang mabuo.
copy.bis: Ganahan magkuyog ang mga kabog — liboan kanila ang mahimong magtigom sa pipila lang ka kahoy, nga mahimong usa ka dako nga pahulayanan.

assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about observing outer parts of plants (leaves, roots, stems) and their role in getting water and nutrients. The card discusses fruit color as a ripeness signal, which is unrelated to plant outer parts or water/nutrient uptake.

copy.en: Lanzones turn yellow and rambutan turn red — that's the sign that they're ripe and ready to eat.
copy.tl: Nagiging dilaw ang lanzones at pula ang rambutan bilang tanda na hinog na ang mga ito.
copy.bis: Ang lanzones mahimong dalag ug ang rambutan mahimong pula isip timaan nga hinog na sila.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the condition for fuel to burn (ignition temperature) but does not describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to temperature changes, such as wood or coal burning. copy.en:
What must happen to fuel before it starts to burn?

It must be heated to its ignition temperature!
copy.tl:
Ano ang dapat mangyari sa panggatong bago ito magsimulang masunog?

Kailangang painitin muna ang panggatong hanggang umabot sa ignition temperature!
copy.bis:
Unsay dapat mahitabo sa sugnod sa dili pa kini mosugod ug sunog?

Kinahanglan painiton una ang sugnod hangtod moabot sa ignition temperature!

copy.en:
Why does the full moon look so round and bright?

At full moon, we see its entire sunlit face, making it look perfectly round and bright!
copy.tl:
Bakit mukhang bilog at maliwanag ang buong buwan?

Sa kabilugan, nakikita natin ang buong mukha nito na naliliwanagan, kaya mukha itong bilog at maliwanag!
copy.bis:
Nganong morag lingin ug hayag ang takdol nga bulan?

Sa takdol, makita nato ang tibuok nawong niini nga nahayagan, mao nga morag lingin ug hayag kini!

copy.en: Phytophthora looks like a fungus but is actually a water mold more related to protists — it caused the Great Irish Famine by destroying potato crops.
copy.tl: Ang Phytophthora ay parang fungus pero water mold pala na mas malapit sa protist — ito ang sanhi ng Great Irish Famine dahil sinira nito ang mga patatas.
copy.bis: Ang Phytophthora morag fungus apan usa diay ka water mold nga mas duol sa protist — kini ang hinungdan sa Great Irish Famine kay giguba niini ang mga patatas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Unlike plants, fungi have no green chlorophyll, so they can't make their own food
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that fungi are not plants because they lack chlorophyll and cannot make their own food. This touches on a characteristic that could be used in classification, but the competency requires using a table to classify living things into the named groups (plants, animals, microorganisms). The card provides no table and does not classify multiple groups; it only contrasts fungi with plants. Thus it does not directly support the required skill.

copy.en:
Are fungi actually plants?

Many think fungi are plants, but they're not! Unlike plants, fungi have no green chlorophyll, so they can't make their own food — they must digest food from other things.
copy.tl:
Halaman ba talaga ang fungi?

Akala ng marami halaman ang fungi, pero hindi! Wala silang berdeng chlorophyll kaya hindi sila gumagawa ng sariling pagkain — kailangan nilang tunawin ang pagkain mula sa iba.
copy.bis:
Tanom ba gyud ang fungi?

Daghan ang naghunahuna nga tanom ang fungi, apan dili! Wala silay berde nga chlorophyll mao nga dili sila makahimo og kaugalingong pagkaon — kinahanglan nila tunawon ang pagkaon gikan sa uban.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Thin gills that make and release thousands of tiny spores!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a fungal structure (mushroom gills and spores) but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups. It only touches on fungi as a topic, not the classification skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Thin gills that make and release thousands of tiny spores!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: Spore production is a form of reproduction, but the card does not describe the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) or explicitly connect spore release to reproduction as a characteristic of living things.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate sexual from asexual reproduction in terms of: a) number of parents involved, and b) similarities of offspring to parents
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions spores but does not differentiate sexual from asexual reproduction in terms of number of parents or offspring similarity. It does not address the required comparison.

copy.en:
What's hiding under a mushroom's cap?

Thin gills that make and release thousands of tiny spores!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nasa ilalim ng takip ng kabute?

May manipis na hasang na gumagawa at naglalabas ng libo-libong maliliit na spore!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang naa sa ilawom sa kalo sa uhong?

Adunay nipis nga hasang nga maghimo ug mopagawas og liboan ka gagmayng spore!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes fungal anatomy but does not address unicellular vs. multicellular organisms, which is the core of G7-L-3. No mention of single-celled or many-celled organisms, so it provides no direct instructional support.

copy.en:
Is a mushroom the whole fungus?

Nope! The mushroom is only the FRUIT of the fungus. Its real body is long hidden threads called hyphae, underground or inside wood. The mushroom pops up just to release spores!
copy.tl:
Ang kabute ba ang buong fungus?

Hindi pala! Ang kabute ay BUNGA lamang ng fungi. Ang totoong katawan nito ay mahabang hyphae na nakatago sa ilalim ng lupa o loob ng kahoy. Lumalabas lang ang kabute para magpakawala ng spore!
copy.bis:
Ang uhong ba ang tibuok fungus?

Dili diay! Ang uhong BUNGA lang sa fungi. Ang tinuod nga lawas niini mao ang taas nga hyphae nga natago sa ilalom sa yuta o sulod sa kahoy. Mogawas lang ang uhong aron mubuhi og spore!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fungi have their own kingdom, Kingdom Fungi
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the importance of the six-kingdom system and the three-domain system of classification of living things
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that fungi belong to their own kingdom and mentions chitin in cell walls, but it does not describe the importance of the six-kingdom system or the three-domain system. It only touches on a classification fact without addressing the competency's focus.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fungi have their own kingdom, Kingdom Fungi
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions fungi as a kingdom but does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups, nor does it cover the required groups such as flowering/non-flowering plants, mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians, and bacteria. The format-required table is absent, so this is at most related.

copy.en:
Is a mushroom a plant or an animal?

Neither! Fungi have their own kingdom, Kingdom Fungi, and their cell walls are made of chitin — not the cellulose that plants have.
copy.tl:
Halaman ba o hayop ang kabute?

Wala sa dalawa! May sariling kaharian ang fungi, ang Kingdom Fungi, at gawa sa chitin ang cell wall nila — hindi cellulose gaya ng halaman.
copy.bis:
Tanom ba o mananap ang kabuto?

Walay usa niini! Naa'y kaugalingong gingharian ang fungi, ang Kingdom Fungi, ug ang ilang cell wall hinimo sa chitin — dili cellulose sama sa tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: grown from Fusarium venenatum fungus in giant fermentation tanks as a meat alternative
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify the products of traditional biotechnology through fermentation (e.g. cheese, soy sauce, vinegar, nata de coco)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes Quorn, a modern industrial fermentation product, but the competency specifically targets products of traditional biotechnology through fermentation (e.g., cheese, soy sauce, vinegar, nata de coco). Quorn is not a traditional fermented food and the card does not support identifying traditional biotechnology products.

copy.en:
What is Quorn made from?

Quorn is made from a fungal protein called mycoprotein, grown from Fusarium venenatum fungus in giant fermentation tanks as a meat alternative.
copy.tl:
Saan galing ang Quorn?

Ang Quorn ay ginawa mula sa mycoprotein, isang protina ng fungi mula sa Fusarium venenatum na pinalaki sa malalaking fermentation tank bilang kapalit ng karne.
copy.bis:
Asa gikan ang Quorn?
